transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm in the right place, and I really don't want to be a burden or sound overly dramatic. But I guess I came in because... well, I've been having some really dark thoughts lately. 

I just keep thinking it would be better if I didn't wake up. I know that sounds awful, I'm sorry. It's just that sometimes I feel like... like dying would be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family, and to my crew at work. I'm trying really hard to push through it, but it's getting difficult. I hope it's okay that I'm sharing that with you... I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so I can get better. Is that helpful?
Did something traumatic happen to you before these thoughts started?

Well, um... I wouldn't call it traumatic, exactly. I mean, other people have it so much worse, and I don't want to sound like I'm complaining. But... I guess it all sort of started about a year and five months ago. 

My husband, he... he hurt his back pretty badly, and it left him mostly housebound. It's just been an adjustment, you know? Taking on more of the load. I really don't want to make it sound like it's his fault, because it's absolutely not, he's wonderful. But that's just around the time I started feeling this way. I hope that answers your question? I'm trying to be as accurate as I can for you.
Do you feel this way mainly because of your husband's injury and everything that changed after it?

I mean... I don't want to blame it on his injury. It's really not his fault at all. It's... it's me. I just... I keep thinking that I'm the reason he got worse, you know? Like I didn't take good enough care of him. And then... well, at work, I feel like I'm the reason my crew lost jobs, and why clients' homes got messed up with the flooring... 

It sounds so silly when I say it out loud, I'm sorry. But I just have this awful feeling like... like I've poisoned everything I've touched lately. And that's why I feel like I deserve whatever bad things happen to me. I know I shouldn't think that way, and I'm really trying not to. I just... I hope I'm explaining this right. Does that make sense? I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic or unusually up, not just your normal self?

Um... no, I don't think I have. I'm sorry, I hope that's not unhelpful. I've never really been the type to be super energetic or... or unusually up. Even before all this started, I was always just kind of steady, you know? Just going to work and doing my best to keep up with everything. 

I mean, I really wish I had more energy these days so I could be more useful to my husband and my crew, but I definitely haven't had any times where I felt unusually high or anything like that. Am I understanding what you mean correctly? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
If your husband had never injured his back, do you think you would still be feeling this depressed?

Oh, um... that's a really good question. I... I honestly don't know for sure. I'd like to think I wouldn't be, because I really try to be a positive person. But... well, the sadness, this really heavy feeling... it's been with me for about a year and two months now. 

It started a few months after his injury, so... I guess they are connected? But again, I really don't want it to sound like I'm blaming him or the situation. It's just... that's just the timeline of when I started feeling so down. I hope it's okay that I don't have a perfect answer for what would have happened otherwise. I'm just trying to give you the exact timeframe so I can be helpful. Does that give you what you need?
If your husband's condition and the work problems were suddenly resolved, do you think you would still feel depressed?

I... gosh, I really don't know. I mean, I want to say yes, that I'd be perfectly fine if all of that just... went away. Because that's what a normal person would say, right? They'd just bounce back. 

But... honestly? I'm not sure if it would just turn off like a switch. Even when we have an okay day, or I get a little good news about work, this... this heavy feeling doesn't really go away. It's like it's stuck to me now. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds so pessimistic, and I really don't want to come across like I'm not trying to get better. I am trying, I promise. I just... I don't know if fixing those things would fix *me* right away. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm beyond help or anything...
Before this started, had you ever gone through another period in your life when you felt depressed like this?

Um... no, I really don't think so. I mean, everyone gets a little sad sometimes, right? Like if a big job installing tile went wrong or something, I'd get stressed or bummed out for a day or two. But I always just pushed through it and went right back to work. 

I've never felt... well, broken down like this before. This is really the first time it's ever been this heavy and lasted this long. I hope that's okay to say. I just... I don't want to make a big deal out of regular bad days from my past, so I want to be clear that this current feeling is completely different for me. Is that the kind of information you need? I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Um... well, I guess maybe a little bit? I... I hate to admit it because it makes me sound so lazy, and I really pride myself on being a hard worker. But... yeah. 

I used to do a lot of things. Like, I'd paint, or I'd cook these really big meals, and I used to always go for a run before my flooring jobs. I even used to show up for theater rehearsals. But lately... it's just... I don't know. It feels like those things are chores from somebody else's life now. I just don't even care if I miss them anymore. 

I feel really awful saying that out loud. I know I should be keeping up with my hobbies and staying active, I really do. I hope that doesn't make me seem like a bad person, or like I've just given up. Is that the kind of example you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you had trouble sleeping lately?

Um... well, my sleep has been... okay, I guess. I mean, I don't want to complain because I know a lot of people have it much worse. 

I've been trying really hard to keep a good schedule, you know? Going to bed at a reasonable hour and everything. I might wake up a little bit here and there, or maybe take a bit longer to drift off, but nothing too terrible, I don't think. I definitely don't want to sound like I'm whining about a few tossed-and-turned nights. 

Is that what you mean? I hope I'm being helpful. I just try to rest as best I can so I can be ready for the next day, even if it's been hard lately.
Have you noticed a change in your appetite lately?

Um... well, I guess my appetite has been a little different, maybe? I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I'm starving myself or doing anything on purpose. I know how important it is to keep my strength up for installing floors. 

But... honestly, most days lately I just kind of... forget to eat until it's really late. Or I'll make something and take a few bites, and I just feel sort of sick to my stomach, so I stop. I feel bad wasting the food, I really do. And, um, I have noticed my work pants have gotten pretty loose recently. I haven't been trying to lose weight or anything, it's just... happening. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound irresponsible with my health. I'm really trying to do better with it. Is that the kind of change you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.
Do you feel that your sadness and guilt are stronger than you would normally expect from what happened with your husband and at work?

Um... well... I don't know if "stronger" is the right word. I mean, I know it's normal to feel bad when things go wrong, and I don't want to sound like I'm throwing a pity party or being dramatic. 

But... I just... I can't stop thinking that I'm the reason my husband got worse. And then with work... the crew lost jobs because of me, and I feel like I just messed up those clients' homes. It's like... like I just poisoned everything I touched. I feel like I deserve whatever bad things happen to me now because of all that. 

I know that sounds really awful, and I'm sorry to lay all that on you. I really try to stay positive, I promise. I just... it's hard to shake that feeling. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not overreacting or answering this wrong.
Do you believe for certain that you truly caused your husband’s worsening and the problems at work?

Um... well... I guess I do. I mean, I really don't want to sound like I'm completely out of my mind or anything, and I know you're just trying to help me sort this out. 

But... yes. I really believe it. I just... I look at everything that happened, and I can't see it any other way. I'm the common denominator, you know? My husband getting worse... the crew losing out on work... the clients' floors being ruined... it's all me. It really feels like I just... like I poison everything I touch, and I can't fix it. I really feel like I deserve all this bad stuff because of it. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds terrible, and I really hope I'm not making things difficult for you by saying that. I'm trying to be reasonable about it all, I really am. Is it okay that I feel that way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the honest truth like you asked.
